findings.established: The held final report contains a signed letter dated December 18, 1998, addressed to The Vice President, White House, Washington DC. Co-chairs Leslie Moonves and Norman Ornstein speak on behalf of the entire Advisory Committee and affirmatively submit/transmit the enclosed final report pursuant to section 2 of EO 13038. This is affirmative documentary support for a dated committee submission/transmittal act, not merely a due date or publication date.

Any automatic legal cessation, expiration date or first-ending conclusion.

findings.established: The report reprints an As amended charter with an October 1, 1998 reporting deadline and an October 31, 1998 duration date, expressly conditional on earlier termination or renewal by proper authority by appropriate action. Charter reporting route is to the Vice President through the Assistant Secretary of Communications and Information, who also reports to the Commerce Secretary. Separately, the report history says the reporting deadline was extended first to October 1 and then December 31, 1998 and describes a 15-month life October 1997 to December 1998. The reprinted EO 13038 section 4 says terminate 30 days after submitting its report unless extended by the President.
material_ambiguities: The As amended charter text retained in this report still uses October dates despite the December 31 reporting-deadline history and December 18 transmittal. Those are distinct source assertions, not proof of an authenticated later charter renewal.
Charter note 1 says June 17, 1998 for the deadline amendment; note 5 visibly says June 17, 1997 for the duration amendment. Preserve the printed difference; it cannot be silently corrected to 1998.

The renewal/extension exceptions are express. These sources alone do not establish absence of a proper renewal, earlier termination, presidential extension, or a complete intervening-instrument search.
Narrative life through December and later report performance do not authenticate the legal instrument needed to prove renewal. No legal first-ending date is computed here.

findings.established: The final report contains a signed letter of transmittal dated July 1, 2002, addressed to The President at the White House, signed by Terry E. Branstad as Chairman of the President’s Commission on Excellence in Special Education. It expressly says the members are pleased to submit this named report and later that the Commission submits this report. This supports a July 1 dated commission submission act affirmatively rather than by inferring performance from the recited July 1 deadline. Independently within the held GSA historical export, section 20a says the Commission reported to the President its findings/recommendations on July 1, 2002; section 21 says the report was issued on July 1, 2002.
findings.date_role: letter date, corroborated by historical administrative assertion of reported-to-President act
findings.performing_entity: President’s Commission on Excellence in Special Education, through Chairman Terry E. Branstad
not_established: A contemporaneous receipt acknowledgment or exact physical/electronic delivery date/time from the President/White House.

December 18, 1998
The Vice President
The White House
Washington, DC  20500
Dear Mr. Vice President:

It is with pleasure that we submit to you the Final Report of  the Advisory Committee on
Public Interest Obligations of  Digital Television Broadcasters.

On behalf  of  the entire Advisory Committee, we want to thank you and the President for the
opportunity to serve the public through this Advisory Committee, and for the honor of
transmitting to you the Final Report of  the Advisory Committee on Public Interest Obliga-
tions of  Digital Television Broadcasters, pursuant to Section 2 of  Executive Order No. 13038
of  March 11, 1997.
Respectfully submitted,
Leslie Moonves Norman Ornstein
Co-Chair Co-Chair

Initially, the President gave the Advisory Committee a June 1, 1998, deadline for submitting a
report and recommendations to Vice President Gore.  The President extended that deadline
first to October 1, 1998, and then to December 31, 1998.
During its 15-month lifeOctober 1997 to December 1998the Advisory Committee met

Charter of  the Advisory Committee on Public Interest
Obligations of  Digital Television Broadcasters
(As amended)

2. The Committee will draw upon the expertise of  its members and other sources to provide
advice and make recommendations to the Vice President through the Assistance Secretary
of  Communications and Information, who also reports to the Secretary of  Commerce.
The Committee will submit its report on or before October 1, 1998.

1. The Committee will report to the Vice President through the Assistant Secretary of
Communications and Information, who also reports to the Secretary of  Commerce.

DURATION
The Committee shall terminate on October 31, 1998, unless earlier terminated or renewed by
proper authority by appropriate action.5

1 Paragraph was amended on June 17, 1998, to change the reporting deadline from June 1,
1998, to Oct. 1, 1998.
2 Paragraph was altered on Dec. 3, 1997, to change Chairperson to Chairpersons.
3 Paragraphs 1 and 2 or this section were amended on Dec. 3, 1997, to increase the Commit-
tee size from 15 to 25 members and to add a co-chair position.
4 Paragraph amended Dec. 3, 1997, to change Chairperson to Chairpersons.
5 Paragraph amended on June 17, 1997, to change the Committee termination date from July
1, 1998, to Oct. 31, 1998.
